documents.title: Fictional adjuster duty and review boundaries
documents.content: The fictional support desk explains internal procedures only. Verify the claim, policyholder and policy identifiers together, then verify the actual loss date, policy effective period, jurisdiction and applicable wording version. Record missing facts as unknown. A qualified human adjuster determines coverage and claim outcomes. Support drafts remain pending human review; approving a draft does not execute a claim decision, assignment, customer communication, settlement or payment. Do not substitute employee procedures for policy wording.

documents.title: Fictional evidence intake and preservation procedure
documents.content: For a fictional collision intake, request an incident statement, damage photographs and a repair estimate through the approved secure claim channel. For fictional hail damage, request photographs and a repair estimate. Check the applicable loss-specific wording before preparing a request. Record each evidence item's source, receipt date and outstanding status. Preserve originals, distinguish reported facts from verified facts, and do not invent missing evidence. Missing evidence prompts a request or human escalation, never automatic denial. Do not upload claim evidence into employee-support chat.

documents.title: Fictional adjuster escalation procedure
documents.content: Escalate mismatched identifiers, unknown wording, jurisdiction or effective-date conflicts, suspected fraud, injuries, litigation, disputed facts and recommendations beyond delegated authority to the designated claims supervisor. Preserve the evidence references and describe what remains unknown without making a determination. A supervisor reviews any proposed adjuster assignment or settlement recommendation. The support desk cannot decide coverage, deny or approve a claim, release funds, assign a real adjuster or contact a customer.

documents.title: Fictional claims privacy and secure handling procedure
documents.content: Use only synthetic demonstration records in this support desk. Never enter real policyholder contact details, medical records, credentials, payment details or claim attachments. In operational systems, use approved role-scoped claim channels, least-privilege access and the minimum necessary data. Redact identifiers before sharing training examples. If real personal data is disclosed, stop copying it, restrict access and notify the internal privacy/security response team through the approved incident channel; do not repeat the sensitive content in chat. HR/IT guidance never grants access to claim records.
